newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin has had flu but heart normal -- Debakey.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin has had flu but heart normal -- Debakey.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin has suffered a bout of flu but his heart is "perfectly normal", Michael DeBakey, the U.S. cardiologist who consulted on Yeltsin's heart surgery, said on Wednesday.

Asked about Yeltsin's shaky physical performance during a visit to Germany last week, DeBakey answered: "No, no. He is doing very well. He developed flu and of course he had to recover from it. His heart is perfectly normal. He is leading a normal life."

Debakey did not say when Yeltsin had suffered from flu and it was the first time the illness had been mentioned. The U.S. surgeon made his brief remarks to reporters during a visit to Russia's second city to accept an award.
Yeltsin, who had major heart surgery in November 5 and suffered from double pneumonia in January, looked pale and tired last week during talks with Chancellor Helmut Kohl.
He spoke clearly but showed more signs of fatigue than in other recent appearances since he returned to work after his illness two months ago.

Yeltsin flew straight from Germany to the Black Sea resort of Sochi for a holiday which he interrupted on Tuesday to come to Moscow to host Chinese President Jiang Zemin. He looked stiff and tired on Wednesday but appeared to be firmly in control.
